text:
ops-bot: RED ALERT: increased KV blockmanager evictions and paging spikes detected in us-west-2 cluster. metric: kv_eviction_rate trending +420% over 10m, paging_io_ops +300%. rolling back not automated.

Maya R: seeing the same on our perf dashboard. latency cliff around 120s requests for long-context chat. a few 502s.

Anil P: any recent deploys to blockmanager / batching?

Devon S: pushed a change to continuous-batching last night to increase prefetch window (`max_prefetch_tokens`) from 128 -> 512 to try to improve throughput for short queries.

Maya R: that aligns timewise. when batching prefetch grows, KV cache usage balloons and block churn goes way up. might be blowing up metadata as well.

Lia C: customer impact: internal telemetry shows 3 enterprise customers with high-volume seq2seq saw sustained request errors and latency. paged-kv queue backed up, 2 customers reported degraded SLAs.

oncall-rotation: oncall taking. starting triage.

Anil P: first mitigation idea: drop prefetch back to 128 immediately to stop cache blowup. can we hotpatch the config?

Devon S: yes. I can push hotpatch to feature flag `cb_prefetch_limit` on production-scale groups. preparing patch now.

Maya R: also reduce `kv_block_size` temporarily? our block manager tends to thrash when blocks are large and many small keys collide. current default is 1MB. lowering to 512KB might reduce eviction amplification.

Devon S: I can flip `kv_block_size` to 512KB for the problematic pool as part of hotpatch. doing one region at a time.

ops-bot: Incident created: INFR-4567. Pager duty notified.

Devon S: hotpatch commands (dry run):
```bash
# set prefetch back
redwoodctl config set --pool inference-prod-usw2 cb_prefetch_limit=128 --target pool:inference-prod-usw2
# reduce block size for pool
redwoodctl config set --pool inference-prod-usw2 kv_block_size=524288 --target pool:inference-prod-usw2
```

Devon S: applying to canary subset now (10%). will monitor.

Maya R: watch eviction_rate, paging_io_ops, and `kv_metadata_alloc` (suspect leak).

Anil P: oncall, if canary stabilizes, roll to 50% then 100%. prepare rollback step if errors increase.

10m later...

Devon S: canary looks good. eviction_rate down 78% on canary hosts, paging_io_ops down 65%. no uptick in errors.

Lia C: customer impact: error counts for the 3 customers dropped ~90% after canary patch. sending update to CSMs.

oncall-rotation: proceeding to 50% rollout.

Maya R: important: we still saw `kv_metadata_alloc` cumulative growth over the last 36h. hotpatch stopped the acute thrash but metadata growth trend remains in the older hosts. might be a separate leak in block metadata retention path.

Anil P: agree — add an immediate GC trigger for metadata if possible. there is a runtime flag `kv_meta_gc_aggressive` we can enable to force reclaim.

Devon S: enabling `kv_meta_gc_aggressive=true` on the pools being rolled. doing a staggered restart for processes that don't pick up the flag dynamically.

Maya R: evidence: memory profile shows many stale `block_ref` objects pinned by `continuous_batcher` entries. I can push a small guard in the batcher to drop references if request timeout exceeded. but that's code change (PR) not hotpatch.

Anil P: ok short term: gc flag + prefetch rollback + block size reduction. medium term: patch batcher to clear refs and add tests.

1h later...

ops-bot: Rollout: 50% -> 100% complete. All target pools patched. No regressed alerts in last 15m.

Devon S: 100% done. eviction_rate normalized, paging down to baseline.

Lia C: CSM update queued: brief incident report, mitigation steps, and ETA for code fix.

Maya R: follow-ups:
- create bug INFR-4568 for metadata leak investigation (batcher refs)
- add an e2e regression test that simulates high prefetch to catch cache blowups
- run load test with `kv_block_size` variants (256KB/512KB/1MB) and capture eviction amplification metrics
- instrument allocation site for `block_ref` to find leak origin

Anil P: add a dashboard panel for `kv_prefetch_active_tokens` so we can alert earlier. add a composite alert: prefetch > 200 && eviction_rate > 50% -> P1.

Devon S: PR for faster ref-drop in batcher started: draft link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/continuous-batcher/pulls/89 (will add unit + integration tests).

oncall-rotation: handing off to next oncall @Anil P for post-incident actions.

Anil P: taking. immediate runbook items assigned:
- verify no residual high-latency traces in APM
- confirm hotpatch config is persisted to infra repo (so new hosts pick it up)
- schedule postmortem tomorrow 11:00am PT with SRE, infra, perf, and customer success

Maya R: also add a quick smoke job that simulates long-context chat every 5m to detect regression earlier.

Lia C: logged customer notification and follow-up calls for the impacted accounts.

Devon S: will follow up with PR and deploy plan for batcher fix.

oncall-rotation: incident transitioning to post-incident monitoring. closing active mitigation channel. :white_check_mark:

Maya R: thanks team. main action items summarized in INFR-4567 and INFR-4568.

Anil P: postmortem owners: Maya (root cause & fix), Devon (code patch), Lia (customer comms).

ops-bot: Incident INFR-4567 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
